title: RAROC, Adjusted RAROC and Hurdle Rate

map.tested: The rare heavily-computational topic inside Operational Risk. Three sub-questions recur: compute RAROC; compute adjusted RAROC (ARAROC); and compute the hurdle rate the RAROC must clear.
map.specifics: Reported variants: '2 on adjusted RAROC'; 'effect on RAROC by changing its components (economic capital, income, expense)': a sensitivity/direction question, not a plug-in; 'find hurdle rate'; 'weighted cost of capital given break-even cost'. Hurdle rate = value-weighted cost of common equity (via CAPM) and preferred equity. The ARAROC adjustment is alpha minus (beta_E x excess market return). The polarity of each component's effect on RAROC is the corruption operator of choice.

vardeezReading: ORR-18: Very Important. CR-5: "LO 23.g for RAROC is important, but RAROC is more important in Operational Risk".

los.text: Define, compare, and contrast risk capital, economic capital, and regulatory capital and explain methods and motivations for using economic capital approaches to allocate risk capital.
los.note: pinned to topic D3 (regulatory vs economic capital), not to this topic

los.text: Describe the RAROC (risk-adjusted return on capital) methodology and its use in capital budgeting.
Calculate and interpret the RAROC for a project, loan, or loan portfolio and use RAROC to compare business unit performance.
Explain challenges that arise when using RAROC for performance measurement, including choosing a time horizon, measuring default probability, and choosing a confidence level.
Calculate the hurdle rate and apply this rate in making business decisions using RAROC.
Calculate the adjusted RAROC for a project to determine its viability.
Explain challenges in modeling diversification benefits, including aggregating a firm’s risk capital and allocating economic capital to different business lines.
Explain best practices in implementing an approach that uses RAROC to allocate economic capital.
Apply risk-adjusted return on capital (RAROC) to measure the performance of a loan.

selectors.name: Compute RAROC
selectors.what: After-tax RAROC = (revenues - costs - expected loss - taxes + return on risk capital +/- transfers) / economic capital, in plain form or with inputs that do not belong (red herrings). Also the loan form of CR-5 g: loan revenues over capital at risk.
selectors.theory: What goes in the numerator and the denominator and why (EL subtracted though no capital is held for it; return on risk capital added; economic, not regulatory or accounting, capital below).

selectors.name: Adjusted RAROC
selectors.what: ARAROC = RAROC - beta x (market return - risk-free rate); accept if it exceeds the risk-free rate; the break-even beta.
selectors.theory: Why the adjustment strips out systematic risk and why the benchmark becomes the risk-free rate for every business line.

selectors.name: Direction of the effect on RAROC
selectors.what: Which way RAROC moves when economic capital, income, expenses, expected loss, funding cost, tax or the confidence level change: a sensitivity question, not a plug-in.

selectors.name: Find the hurdle rate
selectors.what: After-tax weighted cost of common equity (CAPM) and preferred equity at market values; then the accept or reject decision against it.
selectors.theory: What the hurdle is and is not (no debt term, already after tax, market weights), and the flaw of a single hurdle for all projects.

selectors.name: Cost of capital from the break-even
selectors.what: Reverse-solves around the hurdle: the cost of common equity implied by a given hurdle or break-even, or the break-even revenue at which RAROC equals the hurdle.

selectors.name: Interpret and compare RAROC
selectors.source: Vardeez: 'RAROC calculations' on ORR-18 c (calculate and interpret; compare business unit performance)
selectors.what: Given RAROC figures for units, loans or projects, decide which adds value or ranks higher; EVA / NIACC positive exactly when RAROC is above the hurdle.

notSelected: ORR-18 a (risk, economic and regulatory capital: topic D3), ORR-18 b beyond the make-up of the RAROC ratio, ORR-18 d (horizon, PD and confidence-level challenges, unless the question is S3), ORR-18 g (diversification, aggregating and allocating capital) and ORR-18 h (best practices) carry no shape, no Map point and no Vardeez pointer.
